title: Đề thi thử tốt nghiệp THPT — Tiếng Anh 12 (GDPT 2018)
subject: Tiếng Anh
instructions: Read the questions carefully and choose the best option A, B, C, or D. Listening track allows at most 2 plays.

pages.text:
[Audio Track 1: Green Campus Initiative]
Presenter: Welcome to our weekly school sustainability podcast. Today we speak with Lan, student coordinator of the Green Campus Initiative at Binh Minh High School. Lan explains that the team began by placing color-coded recycling bins beside every staircase and organizing monthly repair workshops for broken bicycles and umbrellas.

Urban Community Gardens
In many crowded cities, unused rooftop spaces are gradually being turned into thriving vegetable gardens. Residents work together every weekend to prepare soil beds [1] _____ install rainwater barrels. These shared plots not only supply fresh produce [2] _____ also strengthen social bonds among neighbors of all ages. Schools located nearby often bring students to the rooftops [3] _____ learn practical lessons in plant biology. Although maintaining a rooftop garden requires careful planning, [4] _____ benefits far outweigh the initial cost. Local authorities have begun offering small grants to neighborhoods [5] _____ wish to launch similar projects, proving that sustainable habits can take root [6] _____ in densely populated districts.

Reading Passage 1: Quiet Libraries in a Hyper-Connected World
For decades, public libraries were viewed mainly as silent warehouses for printed volumes. Today, however, neighborhood libraries are reinventing themselves as flexible civic hubs while preserving quiet study rooms. Visitors can borrow audiobooks, reserve soundproof booths for online interviews, or attend free workshops on digital literacy.

Research conducted across twelve municipal branches showed that teenagers visited libraries most frequently when quiet reading zones were paired with collaborative project tables. Rather than replacing printed books, digital catalogs actually boosted borrowing rates because readers could locate niche titles within seconds. Librarians increasingly act as information guides who help citizens verify online sources and distinguish evidence-based reporting from misleading claims.

Reading Passage 2: Coastal Mangrove Restoration and Local Livelihoods
Along tropical estuaries, mangrove forests serve as living buffers that absorb storm waves and trap river sediment before it clouds offshore reefs. Between 1990 and 2010, rapid pond construction cleared wide belts of coastal trees, leaving nearby villages vulnerable to high tides and coastal erosion.

Recent community-led programs have shifted from top-down fencing toward integrated mangrove-aquaculture systems. Under this approach, farmers maintain at least sixty percent natural tree cover around tidal channels, allowing shrimp and mud crabs to feed on fallen leaves without artificial chemical feeds. Field measurements over five years revealed that restored belts reduced wave energy by nearly half while generating steadier household incomes than intensive open ponds. Planners note that long-term success depends on clear land-use agreements and shared monitoring between villagers and marine scientists.

questions.competency: Sequence conversational turns and paragraph sentences logically
questions.stem:
Arrange the turns to make a natural conversation:
a. Mai: Would you like to join our museum audio-guide project?
b. Nam: That sounds great! When do we meet?
c. Mai: Every Thursday afternoon in the media room.
questions.explanation: Invitation (a) -> acceptance and question (b) -> schedule answer (c).

questions.competency: Sequence conversational turns and paragraph sentences logically
questions.stem:
Arrange the turns to make a coherent exchange:
a. Teacher: Have you uploaded your lab summary yet?
b. Minh: Yes, I submitted the PDF five minutes ago.
c. Teacher: Thank you, I will review it before Friday.
questions.explanation: Question (a) -> confirmation (b) -> acknowledgment (c).

questions.competency: Sequence conversational turns and paragraph sentences logically
questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences into a cohesive short note about bicycle commuting:
a. First, dedicated bike lanes keep morning commuters separated from heavy trucks.
b. Riding a bicycle to school benefits both personal fitness and air quality.
c. In addition, covered racks near school gates protect bikes from sudden rain.
d. Therefore, expanding safe cycling routes is a smart investment for towns.
questions.explanation: Topic sentence (b) -> supporting reasons (a, c) -> conclusion (d).

questions.competency: Sequence conversational turns and paragraph sentences logically
questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a logical thank-you email:
a. Dear Dr. Linh, thank you for mentoring our robotics club this term.
b. Your feedback on our sensor calibration helped us reach the regional finals.
c. We would be honored to invite you to our showcase next Saturday.
d. Best regards, Hoang Anh.
questions.explanation: Greeting & thanks (a) -> specific detail (b) -> invitation (c) -> sign-off (d).

questions.competency: Sequence conversational turns and paragraph sentences logically

Arrange the sentences into an informational paragraph about wetlands:
a. As water slows down through dense reeds, suspended mud settles naturally.
b. Freshwater wetlands filter agricultural runoff before it reaches main rivers.
c. Consequently, downstream communities enjoy cleaner water and lower treatment costs.
questions.explanation: Claim (b) -> mechanism (a) -> consequence (c).
